openQuestions.question: ?debug trips the CSP: r3f-perf's embedded Roboto (data:font/woff) is loaded through troika's font loader (a fetch), which connect-src 'self' blocks, so the console logs 'Refused to connect to data:font/woff...' and 'Failure loading font'. The WP-16 report's ?debug spec cannot pass without acknowledging a real CSP violation, so it is not committed. Fix in the debug chunk (for example pass r3f-perf a self-hosted font or turn its text off), then WP-17 adds the spec.
openQuestions.default: No ?debug spec; the item is open.

openQuestions.question: ExhibitDialog's onClose handler closes whatever story is open when the queued 'close' event of the previous dialog close runs. On a busy main thread (SwiftShader, a slow phone) an Esc then Tab and Enter can reopen a story before that event lands, and it closes again at once (seen in the local keyboard walk, trace: /exhibit/finance-tracker/ then back to /). Guard onClose to the id it closed, or ignore a close event while the dialog is open.
openQuestions.default: keyboard.spec waits for the close event before the next Tab.

openQuestions.question: A failed exhibit chunk import also surfaces as an unhandled promise rejection ('Failed to fetch dynamically imported module'), besides the logged 'Exhibit verafin failed; showing the placeholder'. The crate and the card are right. Catch the lazy import's rejection in the kit?
openQuestions.default: exhibits.spec acknowledges exactly that page error.

openQuestions.question: The brief's 8-minute local run target is out of reach since WP-11 (two-worker local run 16.7 min, mostly desktop rail-input walks at about 10 s an arrival). Keep it as a CI-only target (A5) or drop it?

openQuestions.question: A3 needs an update-baselines dispatch on a pushed ref. With the sharded e2e job the dispatch uploads two artifacts, visual-baselines-desktop-rest and visual-baselines-phones-rest; both go into tests/e2e/__screenshots__/visual.spec.ts/ in the commit 'test(visual): baseline slice stops for WP-17'. Until then npm run visual in CI fails on missing baselines for the new visual.spec, so the dispatch must come before the first normal push run is expected green.
